most_similar_reason: Candidate 4 shares the same distinctive episode almost point for point: a god secretly warns a chosen man to build a great boat and load it with living things, a multi-day storm destroys all humanity, the boat grounds on a mountain, birds (including one that does not return) are released to test the waters, and the survivor offers a sacrifice after which the gods make a lasting pledge to him.
least_similar_reason: Candidate 10 concerns a crippled smith's captivity, revenge killings, skull-cups and an escape by flying garment, with no creator god, no destruction of humanity, no vessel of survival, and no covenant or renewal of life.
pair: Genesis flood narrative | Gilgamesh flood myth
